Wadi Ghadir gravity – 3-D density inversion with SimPEG¶

Wadi Ghadir, Eastern Desert, Egypt · complete Bouguer anomaly (ρ = 2.67 g/cm³)

Written by Mohamed Sobh, LIAG (Leibniz Institute for Applied Geophysics)

This notebook inverts the complete Bouguer anomalies of the Wadi Ghadir gravity stations for a 3-D density-contrast model with SimPEG. It is the first of three:

Notebook Data Unknown
06 (this one) gravity stations, complete Bouguer anomaly density contrast Δρ [g/cm³]
07 magnetic readings, total-field anomaly magnetic susceptibility χ [SI]
08 both Δρ and χ together, coupled by a cross-gradient term

All three use the same mesh, topography and data preparation (functions in wghadir/inversion.py), so their models can be compared cell by cell.

The steps

Step Content
1 Load the station anomalies (table 16 of the gravity chain)
2 Separate the regional field of deep sources from the residual
3 Thin the stations (block median) and assign uncertainties
4 Topography and the 3-D tensor mesh; active cells below the ground
5 Survey, forward simulation and sensitivity
6 Smooth (L2) inversion: the reference model
7 Compact inversion: sparse norms solved by IRLS
8 Data fit: observed, predicted and normalised residuals
9 The density model: depth slices and cross-sections; compact against smooth
10 Export (NumPy, UBC-GIF mesh and model, CSV, summary)

Read the results with care. A gravity anomaly can be explained by infinitely many density models. The inversion returns the simplest model that fits the data to their errors, and "simple" is a choice: the compact model (the main result) has the fewest anomalous cells with sharp edges, the smooth model of step 6 the smallest and smoothest contrasts. Both show where mass excess or deficit is likely; depths and shapes depend on that choice.

Each step has ✏️ PARAMETERS (edit and re-run from there), ▶ PROCESSING and 📊 RESULT cells. The complete notebook runs in about two minutes.

1 The station anomalies¶

The gravity chain (notebooks/01_Gravity_Processing.ipynb, table outputs/tables/16_field_stations_relative.csv) provides for every field station the complete Bouguer anomaly relative to base 100, its uncertainty (propagated reading, drift and height errors) and the GNSS position and orthometric height (EGM2008). Terrain effects of the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM are already removed with 2.67 g/cm³; the inversion therefore solves for density contrasts relative to 2.67 g/cm³, and cells of the topography belong to the model.

In [2]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
RHO_REDUCTION = 2.67      # Bouguer density of the reduction (g/cm³): one of 2.00, 2.20, ..., 3.00
SENSOR_HEIGHT_M = 0.25    # CG-6 sensor above the station mark

      f"median uncertainty {grav.sigma.median() * 1000:.0f} µGal; elevations {grav.z.min():.0f}–{grav.z.max():.0f} m")
grav.describe().loc[["mean", "std", "min", "max"], ["cb", "sigma", "z"]].round(3)

2 Regional and residual¶

The complete Bouguer anomaly rises by about 20 mGal from south-west to north-east: the effect of deep crustal structure, far below the depth the stations can resolve. Inverting it would push mass to the edges and bottom of the mesh. It is therefore removed first:

  • "upward" (default): the regional field of notebook 03, the gridded anomaly upward-continued by 3 km (outputs/open_source/Wadi_Ghadir_OpenSource_Grids.nc), sampled at the stations;
  • "polynomial": a least-squares polynomial surface of degree TREND_DEGREE;
  • "none": invert the complete Bouguer anomaly as it is.
In [5]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
REGIONAL = "upward"       # "upward", "polynomial" or "none"
TREND_DEGREE = 1
In [6]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
if REGIONAL == "upward":
    grav["regional"] = W.regional_from_grid(REPO, grav.e.values, grav.n.values)
elif REGIONAL == "polynomial":
    grav["regional"] = W.polynomial_trend(grav.e.values, grav.n.values, grav.cb.values, TREND_DEGREE)
else:
    grav["regional"] = 0.0
grav["residual"] = grav.cb - grav.regional
print(f"regional {grav.regional.min():.2f} … {grav.regional.max():.2f} mGal; residual {grav.residual.min():.2f} … {grav.residual.max():.2f} mGal "
      f"(std {grav.residual.std():.2f} mGal)")

regional -6.16 … 2.89 mGal; residual -8.07 … 6.98 mGal (std 2.70 mGal)

3 Thinning and uncertainties¶

Stations along the wadis are often only 100–200 m apart, much closer than the cells of the mesh. One median per block of BLOCK_M metres keeps the information and removes redundancy (and the occasional outlier). Each block value gets an uncertainty: a floor (FLOOR_MGAL, larger than the measurement error because it also absorbs the regional–residual separation and the discretisation) plus a fraction of the value.

The residual has no absolute level (relative gravity, regional removed), so its median is subtracted. SimPEG's gz points up, so the downward-positive anomaly enters with a minus sign.

In [8]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
BLOCK_M = 400.0           # block-median size (≈ the horizontal cell size)
FLOOR_MGAL = 0.05         # uncertainty floor
PERCENT = 0.02            # plus this fraction of |data|
In [9]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
gb = W.block_median(grav, ["residual", "sigma"], BLOCK_M)
gb["data"] = gb.residual - gb.residual.median()
gb["uncertainty"] = FLOOR_MGAL + PERCENT * np.abs(gb.data)
d_obs = -gb.data.values                            # SimPEG convention: gz positive upward
unc = gb.uncertainty.values
print(f"{len(grav)} stations -> {len(gb)} blocks ({gb.n_block.max()} stations in the fullest block); "
      f"data {gb.data.min():.2f} … {gb.data.max():.2f} mGal; uncertainty {unc.min():.3f}–{unc.max():.3f} mGal")

984 stations -> 481 blocks (8 stations in the fullest block); data -9.43 … 4.25 mGal; uncertainty 0.050–0.239 mGal

4 Topography and mesh¶

A tensor mesh covers all gravity and magnetic data plus a margin (the same mesh is used in notebooks 07 and 08): 400 m × 400 m × 100 m core cells, expanding padding cells to the sides and below. The top of the mesh is the highest point of the Copernicus GLO-30 topography; cells above the ground are inactive (air) and are not part of the model.

In [11]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
CORE_DX_M = 400.0          # horizontal core cell size
CORE_DZ_M = 100.0          # vertical core cell size
N_CORE_Z = 20              # core layers (100 m each) below the top of the mesh
N_PAD_XY, N_PAD_Z = 5, 8   # padding cells, expanding by 1.3
REGION_PAD_M = 1000.0      # margin around all gravity and magnetic data (same mesh in notebooks 06, 07 and 08)
In [12]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
grav_all = W.load_gravity(REPO)
mag_all, FIELD = W.load_magnetics(REPO)
region = W.survey_region(grav_all, mag_all, pad_m=REGION_PAD_M)        # same for both data sets
topo = W.topography(REPO, region)
inside = (topo[:, 0] >= region[0]) & (topo[:, 0] <= region[1]) & (topo[:, 1] >= region[2]) & (topo[:, 1] <= region[3])
z_top = np.ceil(topo[inside, 2].max() / CORE_DZ_M) * CORE_DZ_M
mesh = W.build_mesh(region, dx=CORE_DX_M, dz=CORE_DZ_M, n_core_z=N_CORE_Z, n_pad_xy=N_PAD_XY, n_pad_z=N_PAD_Z, z_top=z_top)
active = W.active_cells(mesh, topo)
n_active = int(active.sum())
print(f"region {(region[1] - region[0]) / 1000:.1f} × {(region[3] - region[2]) / 1000:.1f} km; topography {topo[inside, 2].min():.0f}–{topo[inside, 2].max():.0f} m")
print(f"mesh {mesh.shape_cells} = {mesh.n_cells:,} cells, {n_active:,} active (below the topography); "
      f"depth extent {mesh.h[2].sum() / 1000:.1f} km, top at {z_top:.0f} m")

5 Survey, simulation and sensitivity¶

Each block becomes a receiver at the sensor height above the station (gz, in mGal). The integral formulation computes the gravity of every active cell at every receiver with Choclo's prism kernels and stores this sensitivity matrix G (data × cells) in memory: d = G m.

The sensitivity of a cell decays with depth. Without compensation the inversion would put all the mass right below the stations; SimPEG counteracts this with sensitivity weighting (Li & Oldenburg 1998; directive UpdateSensitivityWeights), which scales the regularisation of each cell by its total sensitivity.

In [14]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
receivers = gravity.receivers.Point(gb[["e", "n", "z"]].values, components="gz")
survey = gravity.survey.Survey(gravity.sources.SourceField(receiver_list=[receivers]))
model_map = maps.IdentityMap(nP=n_active)
sim = gravity.simulation.Simulation3DIntegral(survey=survey, mesh=mesh, rhoMap=model_map, active_cells=active,
                                              engine="choclo", store_sensitivities="ram")
tic = time.time()
G = sim.G
sens = np.sqrt((G ** 2).sum(axis=0))                 # column norms: total sensitivity of every cell
print(f"G: {G.shape[0]} data × {G.shape[1]:,} cells ({G.nbytes / 1e6:.0f} MB) in {time.time() - tic:.1f} s")

G: 481 data × 105,895 cells (204 MB) in 3.3 s
In [15]:
# 📊 RESULT
full = W.model_on_mesh(mesh, active, sens)
v = full.reshape(mesh.shape_cells, order="F")
layer_mean = np.nanmean(v, axis=(0, 1))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 4.5), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1, 1.4]})
axes[0].semilogx(layer_mean, mesh.cell_centers_z / 1000, "o-")
axes[0].set(xlabel="mean sensitivity of the layer [mGal per g/cm³]", ylabel="elevation [km]", title="Sensitivity decays with depth")
x, y, s0, z0 = W.depth_slice(mesh, full, 0.0, 0.0)            # at sea level
m = axes[1].pcolormesh(x / 1000, y / 1000, np.log10(s0), cmap="viridis", shading="auto")
axes[1].plot(gb.e / 1000, gb.n / 1000, "w.", ms=1.5)
axes[1].set(aspect="equal", xlim=(region[0] / 1000, region[1] / 1000), ylim=(region[2] / 1000, region[3] / 1000),
            title=f"log₁₀ sensitivity at {z0:.0f} m elevation", xlabel="easting [km]", ylabel="northing [km]")
plt.colorbar(m, ax=axes[1], shrink=0.8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

6 Smooth inversion (L2): the reference¶

The classical smooth inversion comes first: it shows which structures any model must contain, and its target-misfit solution starts the compact inversion of step 7.

SimPEG minimises

$$\phi(m) = \phi_d(m) + \beta\,\phi_m(m), \qquad \phi_d = \left\| W_d (G m - d^{obs}) \right\|^2, \qquad \phi_m = \alpha_s \|W_s m\|^2 + \alpha_x \|W_x \partial_x m\|^2 + \alpha_y \|W_y \partial_y m\|^2 + \alpha_z \|W_z \partial_z m\|^2$$

  • Data misfit L2DataMisfit, weighted by 1/uncertainty; the target is φ_d ≈ number of data (χ² = 1).
  • Regularisation WeightedLeastSquares: smallness (α_s) and smoothness in x, y, z, all sensitivity-weighted.
  • Optimisation ProjectedGNCG: Gauss–Newton with conjugate gradients, keeping Δρ within BOUNDS.
  • Directives: initial β from the largest eigenvalues (BetaEstimate_ByEig), β cooling (BetaSchedule), Jacobi preconditioner, stop at the target misfit (TargetMisfit), and a log of every iteration.
In [16]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
ALPHA_S, ALPHA_X, ALPHA_Y, ALPHA_Z = 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0
BOUNDS = (-1.0, 1.0)      # density contrast limits [g/cm³]
BETA0_RATIO = 10.0
COOLING_FACTOR = 2.0       # β is divided by this after every iteration
CHI_FACTOR = 1.0          # target misfit = CHI_FACTOR × number of data
MAX_ITER = 20
In [17]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
dobj = data.Data(survey, dobs=d_obs, standard_deviation=unc)
dmis = data_misfit.L2DataMisfit(data=dobj, simulation=sim)
reg = regularization.WeightedLeastSquares(mesh, active_cells=active, mapping=model_map,
                                          alpha_s=ALPHA_S, alpha_x=ALPHA_X, alpha_y=ALPHA_Y, alpha_z=ALPHA_Z)
opt = optimization.ProjectedGNCG(maxIter=MAX_ITER, lower=BOUNDS[0], upper=BOUNDS[1], maxIterLS=20, cg_maxiter=30, cg_rtol=1e-3)
inv_prob = inverse_problem.BaseInvProblem(dmis, reg, opt)
log_l2 = W.iteration_log()
directive_list = [directives.UpdateSensitivityWeights(every_iteration=False),
                  directives.BetaEstimate_ByEig(beta0_ratio=BETA0_RATIO, random_seed=0),
                  directives.BetaSchedule(coolingFactor=COOLING_FACTOR, coolingRate=1),
                  directives.UpdatePreconditioner(),
                  directives.TargetMisfit(chifact=CHI_FACTOR), log_l2]
tic = time.time()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()) as simpeg_log:
    rho_l2 = inversion.BaseInversion(inv_prob, directiveList=directive_list).run(np.zeros(n_active))
seconds_l2 = time.time() - tic
d_pred_l2 = sim.dpred(rho_l2)
print(f"smooth model: {len(log_l2.rows)} iterations in {seconds_l2:.0f} s; φ_d = {log_l2.rows[-1]['phi_d']:.0f} (target {CHI_FACTOR * len(d_obs):.0f}); "
      f"Δρ {rho_l2.min():.3f} … {rho_l2.max():.3f} g/cm³")
log_l2.table

7 Compact inversion (sparse norms, IRLS)¶

A smooth model spreads every anomaly over a large volume with small contrasts. A compact inversion looks for the model with the fewest anomalous cells and sharp boundaries that still fits the data. SimPEG's Sparse regularisation replaces the squares of the L2 norm by ℓp norms (Last & Kubik 1983; Portniaguine & Zhdanov 1999; Fournier & Oldenburg 2019):

$$\phi_m = \alpha_s \sum |W_s m|^{p_s} + \alpha_x \sum |W_x \partial_x m|^{p_x} + \alpha_y \sum |W_y \partial_y m|^{p_y} + \alpha_z \sum |W_z \partial_z m|^{p_z}$$

  • p_s = 0 rewards a model that is zero almost everywhere (compact bodies); p = 1 on the gradients gives sharp edges (blocky); p = 2 everywhere is the smooth model of step 6.
  • The non-quadratic norms are solved by iteratively re-weighted least squares (directive UpdateIRLS): the inversion first reaches the target misfit with L2 norms, then re-weights the regularisation every iteration, each time shrinking the threshold ε below which values count as "zero", while β is adjusted to keep χ² ≈ 1.
  • Compact models concentrate the anomalous mass and reach the bounds, so the bounds must be realistic: ±0.3 g/cm³ spans the contrasts between granite, sediments and mafic rock.
In [19]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
NORMS = (0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)       # p for smallness, ∂x, ∂y, ∂z  (0 compact, 1 sharp edges, 2 smooth)
BOUNDS_COMPACT = (-0.3, 0.3)     # [g/cm³]
MAX_IRLS_ITER = 30                 # IRLS iterations after the L2 stage
IRLS_COOLING = 2.0                 # β cooling during the L2 stage
F_MIN_CHANGE = 1e-3                # stop when the regularisation changes less than this between IRLS iterations
In [20]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
reg_c = regularization.Sparse(mesh, active_cells=active, mapping=model_map, norms=list(NORMS), gradient_type="total")
opt_c = optimization.ProjectedGNCG(maxIter=100, lower=BOUNDS_COMPACT[0], upper=BOUNDS_COMPACT[1], maxIterLS=20, cg_maxiter=30, cg_rtol=1e-3)
inv_prob_c = inverse_problem.BaseInvProblem(dmis, reg_c, opt_c)
irls = directives.UpdateIRLS(f_min_change=F_MIN_CHANGE, max_irls_iterations=MAX_IRLS_ITER, cooling_factor=IRLS_COOLING,
                             chifact_start=CHI_FACTOR, chifact_target=CHI_FACTOR, verbose=False)
log = W.iteration_log()
directive_list_c = [directives.UpdateSensitivityWeights(every_iteration=False), irls,
                    directives.BetaEstimate_ByEig(beta0_ratio=BETA0_RATIO, random_seed=0),
                    directives.UpdatePreconditioner(), log]
tic = time.time()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
    rho = inversion.BaseInversion(inv_prob_c, directiveList=directive_list_c).run(np.zeros(n_active))
seconds = time.time() - tic
d_pred = sim.dpred(rho)
irls_start = irls.metrics.start_irls_iter
def compactness(m):
    """share of the cells holding 90 % of the anomalous 'mass' Σ|m|"""
    a = np.sort(np.abs(m))[::-1]
    return float(np.searchsorted(np.cumsum(a), 0.9 * a.sum()) / len(a))
print(f"compact model: {len(log.rows)} iterations ({irls_start} with L2 norms, then IRLS) in {seconds:.0f} s; "
      f"φ_d = {log.rows[-1]['phi_d']:.0f} (target {CHI_FACTOR * len(d_obs):.0f}); Δρ {rho.min():.3f} … {rho.max():.3f} g/cm³")
print(f"90 % of the anomalous density sits in {compactness(rho) * 100:.1f} % of the cells (smooth model: {compactness(rho_l2) * 100:.1f} %)")

compact model: 38 iterations (8 with L2 norms, then IRLS) in 107 s; φ_d = 519 (target 481); Δρ -0.300 … 0.300 g/cm³
90 % of the anomalous density sits in 8.4 % of the cells (smooth model: 58.4 %)
In [21]:
# 📊 RESULT
it = log.table
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 3.8))
axes[0].semilogy(it.iteration, it.phi_d, "o-", ms=3, label="φ_d")
axes[0].axhline(CHI_FACTOR * len(d_obs), color="k", ls="--", lw=1, label="target")
axes[1].semilogy(it.iteration, it.beta, "o-", ms=3, color="C1")
for ax in axes[:2]:
    ax.axvline(irls_start, color="C3", lw=1, ls=":")
    ax.text(irls_start, ax.get_ylim()[1], " IRLS starts", color="C3", fontsize=8, va="top")
axes[0].set(xlabel="iteration", title="Data misfit"); axes[0].legend(loc="lower left")
axes[1].set(xlabel="iteration", title="Trade-off parameter β")
bins = np.linspace(min(rho.min(), rho_l2.min()), max(rho.max(), rho_l2.max()), 60)
axes[2].hist(rho_l2, bins=bins, alpha=0.6, label="smooth (L2)", log=True)
axes[2].hist(rho, bins=bins, alpha=0.6, label=f"compact (p = {NORMS})", log=True)
axes[2].set(xlabel="Δρ [g/cm³]", ylabel="cells", title="Distribution of the model values"); axes[2].legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

8 Data fit¶

Observed anomaly, the prediction of the compact model, and the normalised residual (observed − predicted) / uncertainty. A good fit leaves normalised residuals of about ±1 without spatial pattern.

In [22]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
obs, pred = -d_obs, -d_pred                         # back to the gravimeter convention (positive down)
nres = (obs - pred) / unc
print(f"compact model: rms misfit {np.sqrt(np.mean((obs - pred) ** 2)):.3f} mGal; χ² = {np.mean(nres ** 2):.2f}; "
      f"{np.mean(np.abs(nres) < 2) * 100:.0f} % of the normalised residuals within ±2")
print(f"smooth model:  rms misfit {np.sqrt(np.mean((obs + d_pred_l2) ** 2)):.3f} mGal")

9 The density model¶

The compact model: horizontal slices at fixed elevations (the ground is at 0–770 m; blank where no data point lies within MASK_M, the model is unconstrained there) and vertical sections. The sections run east–west and north–south through the survey and along the line A–B of notebook 04 (south-western low to the central high). The last figure compares the smooth and the compact model on the same section and slice (each with its own colour scale).

In [24]:

            "W–E": ((34.70, 24.765), (35.00, 24.765)),
            "S–N": ((34.86, 24.68), (34.86, 24.85))}
SECTION_ZMIN_M = -2500.0
MASK_M = 2500.0           # slices: blank cells farther than this from any data point (unconstrained)

10 Export¶

outputs/inversion/: the compact and the smooth model with their mesh as NumPy archive (read by notebook 08), mesh and models in UBC-GIF format (for 3-D viewers such as ParaView or Geoscience ANALYST), the data with predictions and residuals as CSV, the iteration log and a summary.

In [27]:

                    hz=mesh.h[2], origin=mesh.origin, data_xyz=gb[["e", "n", "z"]].values, data_mgal=obs, predicted_mgal=pred,
                    uncertainty_mgal=unc)
